C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 Races McLaren 750S From 45 MPH and Someone Gets Rolled and Walked Hard
8 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Not long ago, we got pretty happy that, at long last, the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube finally went back to spending some quality time around their usual venue, which is Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey, a very nice racetrack that’s been around since it was established back in 1960.
Alas, once again, our happiness was short-lived, as the videographer probably remembered they still had some cool action from the Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event that recently took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York. Traditionally, just like it’s the case with other events like RaceMotive’s 65-mph skirmishes at Pocono Raceway, the format over there is of the roll racing variety – 45 mph in this particular case because, quite obviously, their strip isn’t as long as the massive straight at Pocono.
However, we recently saw a quarter-mile drag race between a white-shaded C8 Chevrolet Corvette, identified as a hybrid performance E-Ray model, and a silver Porsche 911 Turbo, most likely the slightly older 991.2 variety. Needless to say, America proved its supremacy – twice. But now they’re back at 45-mph roll races.
As for the opponents, one is the mighty McLaren 750S, a high-performance V8 sports car from Britain that is bowing out in 2027 to make way for the upcoming new McLaren McL 820 supercar that is also replacing the Artura hybrid. Until it goes away, though, it can still do a lot of damage to the pride of other supercar owners with its 4.0-liter M840T twin-turbocharged V8 packing 740 hp and its lightweight body.
On the other hand, the opponent isn’t something to be trifled with – as the black and menacing McLaren 750S lined up with an equally black and menacing C8 Chevrolet Corvette of the ZR1 variety . The latter is equipped with a 5.5-liter V8 and twin turbochargers, packing a total of no less than 1,064 horsepower.
The advantage seems to be on America’s side, but we all know that McLaren models are more than the sum of their parts – especially when the aftermarket realm also intervenes. Unfortunately, in this case we can’t say for sure because there’s no description beyond the names of the models – and there are also no electronic scoreboards to show us the top speed figures.
Instead, we have to rely on our eyes and the announcer’s judgment. Well, in this case, there was no need for a photo finish as someone got walked and rolled by about two cars! Now, we’re not going to spoil the surprise, so let’s just check out the video embedded below since it’s just half a minute long. So, what do you say – did you expect that outcome or not?
